name: test_schema_service.py
summary: Unit test suite validating SchemaService data type inference and nullable column parsing logic.
purpose: Ensures the SchemaService correctly identifies column data types (float, date) and nullability from tabular datasets, preventing regression in schema extraction behavior and maintaining contract reliability for downstream data processing pipelines.
responsibilities: Verify float data type inference accuracy from sample data
Verify date/datetime data type inference accuracy from sample data
Verify nullable column detection and parsing logic
Validate SchemaService public API contracts under controlled inputs
Provide fast feedback on schema logic changes during development
inputs: Pandas DataFrames or Series with known column types and null patterns
Hardcoded test fixtures representing edge-case data samples
outputs: Assertion results confirming inferred dtype matches expected type
Assertion results confirming nullable flags are correctly parsed
pytest pass/fail status and tracebacks on regression
architecture_notes: This module sits in the app-isolated unit test layer following a modular monolith or service-oriented app architecture (Django-style apps). It tests the SchemaService in isolation, implying the service is a stateless utility or domain service responsible for metadata extraction. The dependency on pandas indicates the dataset domain operates on in-memory tabular structures. Tests are behavior-oriented (grouped by inference concern rather than method name), which improves readability but may indicate missing parameterized coverage. The file location under backend/apps/dataset/tests/ enforces colocation with the domain it validates.
improvements: Replace hardcoded fixtures with parameterized tests to cover mixed-type columns, NaN variants, timezone-aware dates, and empty strings
Expand coverage to include integer, boolean, string, and categorical dtype inference paths
Introduce shared pytest fixtures for common DataFrame patterns to reduce boilerplate
Add negative-path tests for malformed inputs, empty DataFrames, and unsupported formats
Consider property-based testing (e.g., Hypothesis) to validate inference robustness across generated data distributions
Add a test verifying the full schema object structure (not just individual fields) to catch serialization contract drift
